title: Interest, loans and protection: the tools of money
course_title: Financial Literacy and Personal Finance Management

say: Interest, loans and protection: the tools of money.
This is the video for Module 2 of Financial Literacy and Personal Finance Management.
Every loan and savings account runs on a few simple sums. Your phone calculator is enough.
Simple interest is paid only on the original amount, the principal. Save 100,000 naira at 10% a year for 3 years, and you earn 30,000. You end with 130,000 naira.
Compound interest is paid on the principal plus interest already earned. The same money grows to 110,000, then 121,000, then 133,100 naira.
Over 10 or 20 years the gap becomes very large. And compounding works against you in the same way when unpaid loan interest is added to what you owe.
Many loan apps quote a rate per month or per day. A small-looking number becomes very expensive over a year. 2% a month is about 27% a year with monthly compounding.

say: And 10% a month is about 214% a year. Always ask: what is the total I will repay, in naira, and over how long?

say: To see how fast money doubles, divide 72 by the yearly rate. At 12%, about 6 years. If someone promises 30% a month, the money would double every few months. No legitimate business can do that. It is a classic sign of a Ponzi scheme.

say: Finally, check inflation. For example, Blessing earned 5% while prices rose 20%. Her balance grew by 10,000 naira, but she lost about 12.5% of her buying power.

say: With a flat rate, interest is charged on the full original amount for the whole loan. With a reducing balance, interest is charged only on what you still owe.

say: List every debt with its balance, rate and minimum payment. Pay the minimum on all of them, then put extra money on one debt at a time.
Avalanche targets the highest rate first. A loan app at 8% a month costs 4,800 naira a month on 60,000, so it goes first.

panel.heading: Two ways to order your debts

say: Snowball clears the smallest balance first, for motivation. Either way, when one debt is cleared, add its payment to the next.
And your repayments are reported to credit bureaus licensed by the CBN, so paying on time builds your record.

panel.heading: Two ways to order your debts

say: Before you borrow digitally, check that the lender is on the approved list published by the FCCPC.

panel.heading: Digital loans: check before you borrow

cards.d: The FCCPC publishes approved digital lenders on its website. Check before you install any loan app.
Do not give a loan app access to your contacts or photos. Never pay an upfront fee to receive a loan.
Call your lender before a missed payment. Report harassment or threats to the FCCPC.

say: A hospital stay or a fire in a shop can take years of savings in a week. So build protection from the bottom. First, emergency savings.

panel.heading: Build your security from the bottom

say: Second, debt under control.

panel.heading: Build your security from the bottom

say: Third, insurance. Many people pay a small premium, and the pool pays the one who suffers a covered loss. NAICOM licenses insurers. Read what is excluded before you buy.

panel.heading: Build your security from the bottom

say: Fourth, a pension. If you are self-employed, PenCom's Micro Pension Plan lets you contribute amounts that suit you. For example, Comfort, a tailor, pays 5,000 naira a month.

panel.heading: Build your security from the bottom

say: Last, long-term investments such as government bonds or mutual funds, regulated by the SEC. Before you pay anyone, search the name on the matching regulator's website.

panel.heading: Build your security from the bottom
panel.rule: Check the licence. Pay only into the company's registered account.

say: To remember. Turn monthly rates into a yearly picture. Compare loans by total naira repaid. Pay all minimums, then target one debt.
Verify every provider with its regulator. And build from emergency savings upwards.
